Proposal → proof

The QA framework, running on a real Sun.Studio game

Wood Block Journey, HTML5 / Phaser 3. I had no source code and no spec, only the live build. The game went through analysis, test cases and three-tier automation.

32 / 32 automated checks green 47 test cases · 13 layers Python · Pytest · Playwright · OpenCV

Thanh Nguyen (Leon) · QA Manager case study · Sun.Studio

Why Wood Block Journey

I picked the hard case on purpose

If the framework works here, it works on simpler games too.

Canvas  No DOM to hold on to

The whole game is drawn on one WebGL canvas, so no locator can reach a button. This is where most UI automation stops.

Black box  Live production build, minified

No source code, no test hooks, no spec. Everything had to be learned from the running game.

Real portal  Ads, SDK, analytics all live

Playhop / Yandex Games pre-rolls and interstitials appear at random. The same bundle also carries the FB Instant code path.

No spec, so I wrote one down

Observed rules become the test oracle

R-01Piece fits only on empty cells inside the 9×9 boardverified
R-02Full rows, columns and 3×3 boxes clear at the same timeverified
R-03New hand only after all 3 pieces are usedverified
R-04+1 point per placed cellverified
R-05Clear bonus = 18 × groups + 10 × streakneeds GD sign-off
R-06No fit → Second Chance → Game Oververified
R-08A hand never holds two identical piecesverified
R-09Returning player: dashboard → resume the saved boardverified

Open questions for GD / Dev

  • Q-01 Rescue limit, and what happens on reload during the countdown?
  • Q-02 Is ~6 s of "LOADING AD…" before Game Over the intended UX?
  • Q-03 Confirm the scoring formula (R-05)
  • Q-04 Does the dealer guarantee at least one playable piece?
  • Q-05 Can Dev ship a Game Test Bridge in dev/staging builds?

Why a model? The test compares the board with an independent model after every move, not with a screenshot. If a rule changes, we see the mismatch instead of a silently green script.

Step 3 · Automation

The three-tier ladder from the proposal, on a canvas game

Start from the most stable control point. Step down a tier only when the higher one can't reach.

Tier 1 · Game Test Bridge

Read and arrange game state

Board as FEN, score, hand, open screens. Sets an exact board + hand instead of relying on random deals.
# today: QA shim over Phaser
# in-house: dev-owned contract
game.qa("fen")
→ "x/x/x/x/bbbb1bbbb/x/x/x/x l s1,b"
game.arrange(board, hand)
Tier 2 · Scene tree (Poco-style)

Real input, by node

Phaser display list = UI tree. Named nodes, text and cell geometry. Real pointer drags with closed-loop correction.
game.tap_node("PlaySingle")
game.qa("screenTexts", "GAME_OVER_SCREEN")
→ ["48", "48"]
game.place(slot=0, row=4, col=0)
Tier 3 · Image (Airtest technique)

When nothing else reaches

OpenCV template matching, multi-scale, DPR-aware. Finds the PLAY button, screen titles and checks that the canvas isn't blank.
vision.wait_for(page, "title_your_score")
vision.tap(page, "btn_play")
→ Match(score=0.97)

Every tier sits in the same Pytest suite with the same evidence and report. On native Android/iOS builds, tiers 2–3 become Poco SDK / Airtest; the tests and the oracle stay the same.

The rule every test follows

Arrange through the bridge. Act through real input. Assert against the model.

Arrange

Bridge sets the exact board and hand. No random deals, no 5-minute play-throughs to reach a state.

Act

Real pointer drag on the canvas. The driver reads where the piece is during the drag and corrects the pointer, so there are no hard-coded pixels.

Assert

Board == model after the move, score delta == the formula, state transitions read from the game itself.

# tests/test_03_board_rules.py — one real test, unedited logic def test_line_and_box_clears(ready, kind="row+column"): b = rules.empty(); fill row 4 and column 0, leave (4,0) open before = ready.arrange(b, hand("square_1")) # Arrange · bridge expected, cleared = rules.place(b, piece, 4, 0) # oracle · model result = ready.place(0, 4, 0) # Act · real drag assert result["after"]["board"] == expected # Assert · model assert groups_cleared(cleared) == 2

Tap to play

First-time player: 4 tutorial steps

Each step is solved by the model and done with a real drag. The tutorial must award no points and must leave an empty board.

✓ 4 steps · score 0 · 3 pieces dealt
1× · TC-023
Tap to play

Arranged board, one move

The bridge sets row 4 and column 0 one cell short. One drag should clear both at once.

✓ board == model · 2 groups · +47
Recorded run

Scoring streak, then Game Over → PLAY by image

1× · TC-031
Tap to play

Clear, clear, no clear

The score delta is checked against the observed formula on every move: +29, +40, then +4 when the streak resets.

✓ formula holds · flagged for GD (Q-03)
1.6× · TC-043
Tap to play

No fit → Second Chance → PLAY

Ads are blocked, so the rewarded ad fails. The player must still reach Game Over. PLAY is then found by OpenCV only, with no tree and no ids.

✓ not blocked · new game: score 0, empty board

Honest log

What the exercise taught us

✓

A false positive I avoided

The Game Over panel showed "0" at first. It counts up, so it isn't a bug. I checked with real gameplay, and the test now asserts after the animation settles.

!

Test hooks must respect game rules

Injecting two identical pieces made them share one sprite. The real dealer never does that, so the bridge now enforces the same rule (R-08).

◎

The model caught my own test bug

A 3×3 piece at (0,0) completes box 0: +37, not +9. The oracle flagged it before I trusted the test.

⊘

Block ads and analytics in functional runs

Random ads make runs flaky, and test traffic inflates DAU and ad KPIs. Ads get their own suite with test placements.

⚙

Use GPU runners for anything perf-related

The default headless browser uses software GL: ~40 fps and 7 CPU cores. With a GPU it is 60 fps and game-state calls are ~10× faster.

0

No product defect confirmed in this scope

That is a result too. The value is a repeatable net, plus 5 questions that make the spec explicit.

From demo to team practice

What this means for Sun.Studio

The one ask to Dev: a Game Test Bridge contract

My shim reads the internals of a minified build. That is fine for a demo, but it is not a contract. Expose this in dev/staging builds only:

getState() // board, hand, score, screen setState(fen) // arrange any situation seed(n) // deterministic deals forceAd(result) // ok · fail · closed early

Why it pays off for Dev too

  • A bug report carries a FEN, so Dev reproduces the exact board with one call
  • RNG-dependent issues (unfair deals, game-over edge cases) become repeatable
  • The same hooks serve balancing tools, the device lab and the CI smoke gate

Reuse per new game

  • Per game: bridge + rules model, ~1–2 days for a Phaser title
  • Shared: driver, evidence, report, Notion sync, CI
  • Unity / Cocos: Poco SDK + Airtest; tests stay the same

Where it fits in the 90-day plan

  • Weeks 3–4: automation spike on one P0 path ← this is it
  • Two pilot games: P0 suite as the build gate (G2)
  • Results flow into the Notion dashboard
